thread:
maya: Heads up — us-west-2 shared GPU pool is spiking again. p95 queue length jumped ~6x around 09:10 UTC. Looks like multiple tenants causing KV-cache thrash and long tail latencies. dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/cluster/us-west-2
liam: Which tenants are the loudest? any recent deploys?
rachel: Are we still just using global per-tenant max-rps + soft quotas?
maya: Top offenders from logs are tenant_42, tenant_88, tenant_314. No deploys flagged in deploy-bot, looks like traffic pattern shift + large seq models. KV hit-rate for tenant_42 dropped 70% over the window.
sam: Recommending admission shaping at the front door: weighted token-bucket + dynamic weight adjustment based on recent queue length and kv-hit-ratio. That would reduce inflight work before it hits the runtime and thrashes KV.
jun: Agree. Also consider temporarily shrinking per-tenant cache slices for thrashers (reduce prefetch + lower max-kv-alloc) so they don't evict others' hot keys.
liam: Can you sketch the token-bucket config you mean?
sam: Sure — rough example we can test in staging:
```
admission:
  policy: weighted-token-bucket
  global_rate: 5000r/s
  default_bucket:
    rate: 200r/s
    burst: 500
  tenants:
    tenant_42:
      weight: 0.20
      min_rate: 50r/s
    tenant_88:
      weight: 0.05
      min_rate: 10r/s
```
This keeps total bounded while allowing weights to float. We'll add dynamic adjuster that nudges weights every 30s based on p95 queue length and kv_hit_ratio.
maya: Nice. How do we compute the adjuster? any formulas?
sam: Prototype: for tenant i, new_weight_i = clamp(base_weight_i * f(queue_norm) * g(kv_hit)), where f(queue_norm) = 1 / (1 + alpha * queue_len_norm) and g(kv_hit) = 1 + beta * (kv_hit - baseline). Keep min_weight floor e.g. 0.02 to avoid starving control plane traffic.
rachel: Concern: reducing cache allocations + rate at same time will increase RPCs to storage — could spike egress or backend load. Need metrics gating this.
jun: We can gate by KV backend RPS and network egress. If backend_rps > threshold, don't reduce cache further; instead prioritize admission.
eng-sre-oncall: ops-bot alerted: [ALERT] us-west-2 shared-pool gpu_util > 90% (5m) — incident linked: https://incidents.internal/1917654321
ops-bot: Auto-note: rolled up metrics for last 30m: gpu_util=92%, p99_latency=2.3s, p95_queue_len=48, total_inflight=7.4k
liam: Plan proposal: 1) deploy weighted-token-bucket to 10% of hosts in us-west-2 (canary) 2) enable dynamic weight adjuster in monitor-only mode (log-only) for 1h 3) if stable, flip to enforce and reduce per-tenant cache for top 3 thrashers 4) run for 4h and roll back if backend_rps or egress > 15% above baseline
maya: Metrics to watch during canary: p95_queue_len, p99_latencyp50, gpu_util, kv_hit_rate_per_tenant, storage_backend_rps, egress_bytes/s, error_rate (429/503).
jun: Add one more: tail_kv_evictions and model_kv_miss_cost estimate (tokens/sec wasted).
liam: Who owns the PR and the runbook change?
rachel: I can own the PR for admission config + rollout script. Will include a quick toggle flags: --canary-hosts=10% and --monitor-only.
maya: I'll update runbook and dashboard panels. sam can you own the adjuster code + tests?
sam: Yep. I'll open PR for the adjuster with unit tests and a small sim harness.
eng-sre-oncall: :eyes: please ping if any alert rate changes.
ops-bot: Reaction: :thumbsup: recorded
liam: Quick note — ensure we include an escape hatch: immediate global-rate cut to 40% if p99 > 5s or gpu_util > 98% for 2m.
maya: Agreed. Also add a soft-grace period to avoid flapping (hold decisions for 60s).
jun: After successful canary, we should schedule a wider rollout but keep tenant-weight decay to avoid rapid oscillations.
rachel: One more risk: cross-AZ tenants may have different latencies; ensure weights are applied per-region to avoid punishing remote-origin tenants.
sam: We'll scope the rollout to region-local weights and document that in PR.
maya: Action items: rachel -> PR for config + flags; sam -> adjuster PR + sim; maya -> dashboard + runbook; jun -> cache eviction tuning proposal. Target canary start: 2026-04-09 14:00 UTC.
liam: :rocket: good plan.
ops-bot: Reminder set: canary start 2026-04-09 14:00 UTC (autoreminder to #eng-infra)
